Title: Tycho Crater
Content: Tycho is an impact crater located in the southern hemisphere of the `text(Moon)`. It has a diameter of `text(53 miles)` and is `text(one)` of the most visible craters on the `text(Moon)`. Ejecta, material thrown from the crater upon impact, can be seen as light-colored rays coming from the crater. Some rays are `text(900 miles)` in length. This light coloration is due to Tycho's “young” age. `text(Moon)` rocks thought to be ejected from the impact have been brought back to `text(Earth)` by the Apollo `17` mission and found to be `text(108 million years)` old. Based on rocks brought back by other Apollo missions, many craters on the `text(Moon)` have been dated to be `text(3.9 billion years)` old and are darker in color than more recently formed craters. The floor of the Tycho crater shows evidence of rocks that were heated to such high temperatures during the impact that they melted, then cooled and solidified on the surface.
